faq.q: Does a developer's request to arrange a mortgage count as notice to take delivery?
faq.a: That depends on the letter and the condition of the property. In this case the letter concerned the loan, without saying the home was ready for use. Utility connections and later inspection records did not support the developer's account, so the court did not accept it as the contractual handover notice.

faq.q: Is the notice period four or six months after the occupancy permit?
faq.a: The four months in this judgment came from the parties' contract. Point 15 of the current mandatory standard terms for presale home sales requires the seller to notify the buyer of handover within six months after receiving the occupancy permit. The applicable rules at the time of contracting and the actual agreement still need checking; four months is not a universal period.

faq.q: Can I ignore the developer's notice while the mortgage is still being processed?
faq.a: A pending loan is not by itself a reason to ignore a notice. Payment, loan documents, inspections and handover have their own contractual requirements. Identify the obligation and deadline in the letter, then compare the bank's records with the property's condition. This judgment does not give every buyer a right to stop paying.

edits.before: summary: "The Taipei High Administrative Court set aside a civil servant's dismissal and the review decision after examining a predetermined outcome, missing opportunities to respond and conflicting findings. Private employers operate under a different legal framework, which requires protective measures alongside a fair investigation."
edits.after: summary: "A Taiwan court set aside a civil servant's dismissal over procedural defects. Private employers must protect complainants and conduct fair investigations."

old_metadata.title: Punishment Announced Before Deliberation: A Taiwan Workplace-Bullying Case
old_metadata.seoTitle: Taiwan Workplace Bullying: A Dismissal Set Aside
old_metadata.summary: The Taipei High Administrative Court set aside a civil servant's dismissal and the review decision after examining a predetermined outcome, missing opportunities to respond and conflicting findings. Private employers operate under a different legal framework, which requires protective measures alongside a fair investigation.
old_metadata.author: legal-ai-assistant
old_metadata.featured_image_alt: A round table, plain document folder and three chairs in an empty meeting room

faq.q: Does setting aside the dismissal mean the court found that no bullying occurred?
faq.a: No. The court identified problems in deliberation, the opportunity to be heard and factual findings, then set aside the original disposition and review decision. That does not establish that every alleged act was nonexistent. The court's announcement states that an appeal was possible.

faq.q: Must a company wait for the investigation to end before protecting the complainant?
faq.a: Protection and a fair investigation can proceed together. The Occupational Safety and Health Act requires appropriate action according to how the employer learned of the incident. On receiving a complaint from a worker subjected to bullying, the employer must take measures to prevent further bullying, provide counselling, assistance and protection according to need, and investigate.

faq.q: Can HR copy the procedure from this civil-service judgment?
faq.a: The case concerned civil-service performance assessment and dismissal. Private employers must work under the occupational-safety rules, employment laws and contracts applicable to them. The court's treatment of predetermined conclusions, missing responses and inconsistent evidence helps assess investigation quality; it does not replace the applicable legal framework.

edits.after: seoTitle: "Taiwan EV Chargers: Shared Areas and Consent"

edits.before: summary: "A resident's charger used a shared wall, ceiling and electrical panel. The Kaohsiung court upheld removal and restoration under the common-area rules and the building's bylaws. The installation route, the rights over each part and the required consent all mattered beyond the parking space itself."
edits.after: summary: "A Taiwan court ordered an EV charger removed from common areas. The wiring route, owners' resolution and building bylaws determined the consent required."

old_metadata.title: The Wiring Left the Parking Bay: Why a Taiwan Court Ordered an EV Charger Removed
old_metadata.seoTitle: Taiwan Apartment EV Chargers: Wiring and Consent
old_metadata.summary: A resident's charger used a shared wall, ceiling and electrical panel. The Kaohsiung court upheld removal and restoration under the common-area rules and the building's bylaws. The installation route, the rights over each part and the required consent all mattered beyond the parking space itself.
old_metadata.author: legal-ai-assistant
old_metadata.featured_image_alt: An electric car connected to a charger on a garage column, with conduit running up to an overhead cable tray

faq.q: Can I install a charger and wiring because the parking space is for my use?
faq.a: The equipment's location and the full wiring route still need checking. This installation used a shared wall, ceiling and electrical panel. The court considered that scope, the law and the building's bylaws, and rejected the argument that the work was merely additional wiring in an area for exclusive use. The layout and bylaws of another building may require a different assessment.

faq.q: Does switching off and locking the charger remove the obligation to dismantle it?
faq.a: The resident said the equipment was no longer used and was locked, and offered to give the key to the management committee. The court held that even if those assertions were true, they would not remove the duty to dismantle the installation arising from the breaches of the common-area rules and bylaws. It did not decide that removal is the only possible outcome in every charger dispute.

faq.q: Can a government subsidy replace the building's consent?
faq.a: Subsidy eligibility and permission to use common areas are separate. The 2026 Kaohsiung program discussed here included EV charging cable trays in common areas, but its September 30 application deadline had passed. That policy did not itself authorize an individual resident to carry out work in shared areas.

old_metadata.title: Coins Remained, but the Paid Points Were Gone: A Taiwan Game Refund Claim
old_metadata.seoTitle: Taiwan Game Refunds: Coins and Unused Paid Points
old_metadata.summary: A player sought NT$243,548 for coins left in a game account. The Keelung court treated them as chips used in play, rather than unused paid points or refundable game fees. Current standard terms still protect refunds of unused paid points or game fees after termination, subject to their conditions.

old_metadata.featured_image_alt: A game controller, laptop showing an abstract game, plain colored tokens and closed notebooks on a desk

faq.q: Does calling an in-game balance coins mean it cannot be refunded?
faq.a: The name does not decide the issue. The coins in this case were used as chips in play, and the court held that they were not unused paid points or refundable game fees. For another game, their acquisition, purpose, actual use and contractual treatment need to be examined.

faq.q: Am I unable to end the contract after the first seven days?
faq.a: The current standard terms allow a consumer to notify the operator of termination at any time. Unused paid points or unused game fees must be refunded after necessary costs are deducted within 30 days after termination, or handled in another mutually agreed way. This is separate from the right to cancel in writing within seven days after starting play, without giving reasons or bearing costs, and seek return of unused purchased paid points.

faq.q: Can the contract say that only the operator's records count in a dispute?
faq.a: The current prohibited terms bar a clause making the operator's saved game history and electronic data the sole basis for deciding a dispute. Players can retain payment records, screenshots and support correspondence, and request their own game history to trace the balance. This does not mean that all records held by the operator lack evidential value.
